transcript:
Header: Roadmap Launch Readiness + Incident Review
Date/Time: 2025-11-12 09:15 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Nambiar, Ethan Park, Lena Hoffman, Arun Singh
Links referenced: launch checklist (docs/internal/launch-checklist.md), incident postmortem draft (link: s3://redwood/postmortems/2025-11-05-degraded-traffic), canary runbook (link: /playbooks/canary-runbook)

[00:00] Maya: alright everyone thanks for joining um we wanted to keep this tight 45-ish minutes but we have a lot to cover so i'll kick off with quick context. last week we saw that degraded traffic incident on 11-05 that impacted some Dedicated pools, latency spikes, and a few timed-out requests. priya can you give the quick incident summary?

[00:28] Priya: yeah, sure, so timeline quick - at 03:40 UTC load spiked from a client that hit a bad path in our autoscaler, the scale down/scale up loop caused K V cache thrashing, then a short window where node provisioning lagged - we had about 12 minutes of elevated tail latency, some 504s for the most aggressive qps, this was mostly confined to a single region and Dedicated pool but degraded routed requests to fallback models too so user impact visible.

[01:05] Diego: and just to be clear the root cause was the autoscaler not honoring the min-capacity flag under this combination of burst and long-latency startup? i saw the postmortem draft but wanted confirmation.

[01:24] Priya: right, it's a race in the scale decision code path when we have rapid burst + cold model loads, autoscaler decided scale-to-zero segments too aggressively, then on rehydrate we saw KV cache misses, cold starts, etc. patch is small but we want tests.

[01:46] Ethan: i reproduced locally with the repro harness - adding a 30s stabilize window reduces flapping but we need to consider cost impact. 30s stabilize means higher sustained capacity for short bursts.

[02:10] Maya: tradeoff: latency SLO vs unit cost. for the launch we prioritize customer experience, so leaning towards safety. diego where are we on the bugfix?

[02:28] Diego: PR open, two approvals but want to run canary - i'm proposing a staged deploy: patch to staging, then a 1% canary in prod for 2h, then 10% for 4h, monitor tail latency and error budget. we need a rollback plan though if the patch has unforeseen regressions.

[02:54] Priya: rollback is straightforward, we have a disable flag on the autoscaler path and a retrace step to rebalance KV assignments. but we should also update the runbook to include the new stabilize window param and the exact observability checks (p90/p95/p99 latency, node provisioning time, error rate).

[03:20] Lena: on the launch checklist front i've updated the doc with vendor sign-offs and compliance items but i flagged the incident and added a gating criterion: no unreconciled incident postmortems and two successful canary dry-runs.

[03:40] Maya: perfect that's what we wanted. priorities this week: patch + canary, run long-load tests, update runbook, stakeholder sign-off. arun any QA concerns?

[04:00] Arun: yeah, regression surface is around KV cache edge cases and cold-starts; i'll add deterministic regression tests to the CI that target high token churn and long prefix reuse. also i'll validate model variant fallback behaves correctly under the patch.

[04:22] Diego: quick note - we observed one oddness where the hosted fallback route increased token cost by 8% during the event because more requests fell through to the larger variant. we should add cost-monitoring to canary success criteria.

[04:40] Ethan: good call, i'll add cost-per-request and token-ratio metrics to the dashboard: token-cost, rps, p95 latency, model-switch counts. link to dashboard after this.

[05:05] Maya: on timeline, the roadmap launch is planned week of 2025-11-25. we have about two weeks to finish remediation and run the smoke/dry runs. are we comfortable with that timeline if we target safety first?

[05:28] Priya: if we prioritize safety, yes, but that means our canary needs to be completed by 2025-11-20 to allow rollback and extra QA.

[05:40] Diego: agree. i'll aim to have the patch staged by 2025-11-15 and canary window 11-17 to 11-19.

[06:00] Lena: i'll push for execs to sign off by 11-21; need the runbook and test results to be attached.

[06:15] Maya: ok next topic security/compliance checklist - any open items? we got SOC2 readiness almost done but KMS key rotation doc is still pending?

[06:30] Ethan: KMS rotation steps are documented but we didn't add the new private deployment variant in the doc yet, i'll update the doc and share link. we should also confirm audit log retention for Dedicated customers matches the enterprise add-on.

[06:48] Priya: also SAML SSO test account needs a smoke test as part of launch routine, lena can you coordinate with security?

[07:00] Lena: yes i'll coordinate and add it to the checklist with a hard pass/fail column.

[07:15] Maya: action items recap in a sec but i want to talk about the canary success criteria. what are measurable pass/fail metrics?

[07:30] Ethan: pass if p99 latency stays below 300ms for hosted and below 450ms for Dedicated pool, error rate <0.1%, token-cost variance <5% vs baseline, no unplanned model fallback events, node provisioning median <20s. also we should check cold-start tail percentiles.

[08:00] Diego: add monitoring for autoscaler decisions: scale-up time, scale-down frequency, and min-capacity honors. if any of those exceed thresholds we'll auto-abort the canary.

[08:20] Priya: i'll add alert runbook steps for auto-abort and manual abort. note: the first canary should run in eu-west to hit the same infra profile that saw the incident.

[08:38] Maya: good - schedule wise diego will schedule canary in eu-west per plan. diego, ethan, priya please coordinate on the dashboard and runbook updates.

[08:50] Arun: a quick QA ask - for the load test can we simulate both hosted and dedicated routing variations? i want to ensure routing policies don't unexpectedly shift traffic.

[09:05] Ethan: yes, the harness can do routed mixes, i'll set up a 70/30 split and also test forced fallbacks. i'll produce graphs for token cost and latency distribution.

[09:25] Maya: anything else on incident learning? Priya, do we think the postmortem draft is sufficient for execs or do you want a longer writeup?

[09:40] Priya: draft is ok but i'll add a short executive summary and mitigation timeline. will tag action items in the doc.

[09:55] Diego: also small note for product - we should consider adding a minimum node reserve for high-risk customers as an optional setting, this would avoid cold starts for critical customers during bursts. it costs more but gives stronger SLOs.

[10:15] Lena: product ops will add that as a feature idea and price estimate for GTM.

[10:30] Maya: wrap-up: recap actions — priya update runbook and postmortem exec summary; diego finish PR and schedule canary; ethan run load tests and dashboard; arun add regression tests; lena update checklist and coordinate SSO tests; maya will send roadmap slide and risk register to execs.

[10:56] Maya: okay thanks everyone i'll follow up with an email with notes and links, meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
